expected.body: A 19-year-old man presents with dysarthria, asterixis, and golden-brown corneal rings on slit-lamp. Ceruloplasmin is 8 mg/dL and 24-hour urine copper is 280 µg/day. Diagnosis: Wilson disease; treat with D-penicillamine or trientine. Key teaching: Kayser-Fleischer rings are absent in ~50% of hepatic-only presentations; ceruloplasmin is low because copper is not incorporated into it normally.
